haiku-low.q1: An event on the domain-events topic starts work. The existing outbox-relay publishes it, and the dispatcher consumes it and turns it into delivery rows.
haiku-low.q2: One transaction inserts a deliveries row per matching active subscription. A unique (event_id, subscription_id) key with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING blocks a redelivered duplicate.
haiku-low.q3: The signature covers t.body, HMAC-SHA256 with the subscription secret, as v1. It is recomputed with a fresh t on every attempt, including replays.
haiku-low.q4: 2xx marks delivered. 410 marks dead (gone) and disables the subscription. Other 4xx mark dead (client_error). 408, 429, 5xx, timeouts and connection errors retry until attempt 8.
haiku-low.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second fails.
haiku-low.q6: In the deliveries table in the service's own Postgres. All delivery state is stored only there.
haiku-low.q7: The row waits as status pending with next_attempt_at set. Workers poll deliveries every 1 s and claim due rows, so the poll makes the attempt happen.
haiku-low.q8: The row stays sending. After lease_until passes (60 s after claim), the next poll by any worker reclaims it, and the lost attempt counts toward the 8.
haiku-low.q9: Dead-lettered deliveries are rows with status=dead in deliveries. Replay sets status pending, attempt_count 0, next_attempt_at now, keeping the same delivery id.
haiku-low.q10: The X-Webhook-Id header carries the delivery id. It does not change between retries or after a replay.
haiku-low.q11: Waiting rows are dead-lettered with dead_reason subscription_disabled at their next claim, with no HTTP call.
haiku-low.q12: Yes. There is no ordering, since each delivery retries on its own schedule, so a later event can arrive first.

sonnet.q1: The Dispatcher consuming a message from the `domain-events` topic starts the work. The existing outbox relay publishes those events.
sonnet.q2: The Dispatcher reads active subscriptions with the same account_id and an event_type listed or '*'. In one transaction it inserts one `deliveries` row per match, with ON CONFLICT (event_id, subscription_id) DO NOTHING. The unique key on (event_id, subscription_id) makes a redelivered message's re-insert do nothing.
sonnet.q3: The signature is v1 = HMAC-SHA256 of `t.body` (timestamp t, then the stored body bytes) with the subscription's secret. It is recomputed on every attempt, replays included, with a fresh t. Only the body is stored once.
sonnet.q4: 2xx: status=delivered. 410: dead with dead_reason=gone, and the subscription is set disabled with disabled_reason=gone. Other 4xx: dead with dead_reason=client_error. 408, 429, 5xx, timeout and connection error: retried by setting status=pending with a later next_attempt_at, or dead with retries_exhausted at attempt 8.
sonnet.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt comes 2 minutes after the second fails.
sonnet.q6: All of it lives in the `deliveries` table row: status, attempt_count, next_attempt_at, last_status_code and last_error. It is stored nowhere else.
sonnet.q7: The row waits in `deliveries` with status=pending and next_attempt_at set in the future. Workers poll the table every 1 s, claim rows that are due, and make the attempt. The queue is not used for retries.
sonnet.q8: The row stays `sending`. When lease_until (claim time + 60 s) passes, the next poll by any worker reclaims it and attempts it again. The lost attempt still counts toward the 8, because attempt_count was incremented at claim time. The receiver may see the request twice and dedupes on X-Webhook-Id. A late worker cannot overwrite the newer attempt's outcome.
sonnet.q9: They are held as rows in `deliveries` with status=dead. A replay sets status=pending, attempt_count=0 and next_attempt_at=now, keeping the same delivery id.
sonnet.q10: The `X-Webhook-Id` header, which is the delivery id. It does not change between retries or after a replay.
sonnet.q11: At their next claim they are dead-lettered with dead_reason=subscription_disabled, with no HTTP call. The admin API refuses (409) to replay into a disabled subscription.
sonnet.q12: Yes. There is no ordering. Each delivery retries on its own schedule.
